note: Every PASS is backed by an executed test in this run. Layers: A=live core, B=candidate (not wired), C=specification-only.

capabilities.limitation: Required metadata for issuance: recorder (recorder is a TII-Core required field per SPEC §5). No other field required. identifier_status is hard-set to "test" (src/ledger.js:92) — there is no production issuance code path at all.

capabilities.codePath: src/ledger.append, src/projection (ignition treated as any other module bucket)
capabilities.test: three TIIs (none / one / full lifecycle + reclassification); verify all three project as valid

capabilities.capability: §9 Transition optionality — TII valid with 0 / 1 / (described→disputed→withdrawn→reintroduced) transition records; and reclassifiable as "wrong vocabulary"
capabilities.codePath: src/ledger.append, src/projection (transition treated as any other module bucket)
capabilities.test: three TIIs (none / one / full lifecycle + reclassification); verify all three project as valid
capabilities.observed: A has no transition section=true; B has transition=true; C transition record count=4; C also has a 'reclassification' module=true; verify.ok=true

capabilities.capability: §10 State non-primitivity — record A/B + transition, then a later interpretation rejecting the discrete-state split; both remain visible
capabilities.codePath: src/ledger.append, src/projection (state buckets + interpretation list are independent)
capabilities.test: two state records + transition + an interpretation.revised event rejecting the split
capabilities.observed: both state records still present=true; current interpretation says continuous process=true
capabilities.limitation: Partial by design of the DISPLAY: the resolution page still renders the historical State A / State B sections (they have records) alongside the current interpretation. There is no "state concept withdrawn" flag that hides them — nor should there be, since the history must stay visible. The current interpretation does not preserve discrete-state ontology; the historical description does.

capabilities.capability: §11 Address / Domain — 1/many/none/unreachable/replaced/competing addresses; domain add/change/contest/remove; address⊥domain; addr-without-domain; domain-without-address
capabilities.codePath: src/ledger.append, src/projection (address and domain are separate top-level module buckets), src/views (Address / Domain section, "no address privileged" note)
capabilities.test: 9 events covering every address/domain sub-case; inspect projection
capabilities.observed: address buckets=4, domain buckets=2; a1 withdrawn=true; current addresses=["https://host-2.test/x","https://host-3.test/x","https://host-4.test/x"]; the identifier is never derived from any address value
capabilities.limitation: None functional. Address and Domain are fully independent modules. The resolution page shows every current address with its kind and the note "No address is designated as permanently or exclusively authoritative." "Competing addresses" are simply two current address buckets — the system does not adjudicate.

capabilities.capability: §12 Mirror — record with multiple resolvable locations; primary lost; other remains; no re-issuance; old address in history
capabilities.test: two address records + a stop on the primary; check the mirror is still current and the primary is in history
capabilities.observed: primary address has 2 history records=true; mirror still current=true; tii unchanged & earlier ledger bytes are a prefix=true
capabilities.limitation: The address module records locations. The system does not itself probe reachability or fail over; a resolver / client would choose among the current addresses.

capabilities.capability: §13 Content hash — digest A → change a byte → digest B; root TII unchanged; both hashes visible; not claimed byte-identical. Reverse: equal hashes in two TIIs do NOT merge them
capabilities.test: record two successive sha256 digests on one TII; record the same digest on two separate TIIs
capabilities.observed: both digests in history=true; root identifier unchanged=true; equal-hash TIIs stay separate (3 distinct TIIs)=true
capabilities.limitation: The system records content-verification values as data. It never (a) claims byte identity from a matching hash, (b) merges identifiers because their content hashes match, or (c) changes a TII because content changed. It also does not itself compute or check the digest of any external artifact — that is the recorder's assertion (see bin/tii.js hash-file for a helper).

capabilities.capability: §14 Series / lineage — one lineage → split → contest → merge → reject lineage entirely; recorded as revisable judgment
capabilities.codePath: src/ledger.append, src/projection (series is a normal module bucket; SPEC frames it as a judgement not an object)
capabilities.test: 5 series events covering the full revision arc
capabilities.observed: series bucket records=5; disputed=true; withdrawn=true; current=null
capabilities.limitation: Series/lineage is a module bucket like any other. Members are just data (arrays of strings). The system does not cross-link the named member TIIs or build a graph — lineage is a local, revisable judgement recorded on this TII.

capabilities.capability: §15 Branch / merge — A→B→(C1,C2)→D; ancestry preserved; branch records survive merge; projection derived not canonical. Cyclic descriptive references
capabilities.test: construct a branch/merge lineage as events; add a cyclic transition relation
capabilities.observed: lineage-node records=2; series records=2; cyclic relation_kind accepted=true; verify.ok=true
capabilities.limitation: There is NO graph/branch/merge engine. "Branch" and "merge" are just event_type strings + series module records; ancestry is whatever the events say. There is no visual projection of a DAG (the resolution page lists records, it does not draw a tree). Cycles are neither detected nor forbidden nor warned about — the engine has no concept of a graph to find a cycle in. SPEC frames cycles as a candidate relation_kind value only.

capabilities.capability: §16 Ownership decomposition — no owner field; separate stores/controls/may_modify/... relations with different, changing actors; overlap + conflict + history retained
capabilities.codePath: src/ledger.append, src/projection (relation module; no owner concept anywhere in the core)
capabilities.test: 9 distinct relation types + an actor change + a disputed relation
capabilities.observed: no owner anywhere=true; 9 concurrent relation buckets; 'stores' has 2 history records=true
capabilities.limitation: None. The core has no owner field. Relations overlap and conflict freely; the system records, it does not resolve. Stewardship change (below) is just another relation/event and never touches the TII.

capabilities.capability: §17 Stewardship transfer — A→B→C with dates, evidence, a contested then accepted transfer; TII never changes
capabilities.layer: A (live core) for storage; SPECIFICATION-ONLY for a dedicated transfer workflow
capabilities.test: 3 stewardship events including a dispute; check history + that the identifier is unchanged
capabilities.observed: 3 stewardship records retained=true; identifier unchanged=true; verify.ok=true
capabilities.limitation: PARTIAL: a stewardship transfer is fully recordable as append-only events and the TII is provably unchanged. But there is NO first-class transfer procedure in the live code — no `authority.transferred` handling in projection, no signature/authorization check, no "current steward" derived field, no succession-kit generation. spec/governance-candidate.md and spec/succession-policy.md describe the procedure; the software only stores the events.

capabilities.capability: §18 Localization stress — ja source + en v1 + en correction + fr + de + later ja annotation; authored unchanged; newest en projected; static build does not mutate; exports keep all; new language needs no schema migration
capabilities.layer: A (live core) — localization IS wired into the live projection + views
capabilities.test: 6 events (source + 4 translations + annotation); check displayContent per language, authored immutability, static-build ledger stability
capabilities.observed: en projected = latest correction=true; ja falls back to authored=true; fr projected=true; authored event unchanged=true; buildStaticSite left ledger byte-identical=true; all 4 translation events in export=true
capabilities.limitation: None. A 5th/6th language is added by appending another localization.added event — no core field, no migration. Translation kind (literal/interpretive) is recorded. The <details> audit trail on the resolution page always shows the authored content.

capabilities.capability: §19 External identifiers — DOI/ARK/ISBN/URL/IPFS-CID/unknown coexist; one disappears without invalidating TII; TII not subordinate to DOI/ARK; unknown types retained
capabilities.codePath: src/ledger.append, src/projection (references[] from external_identifier module + event.external_refs), src/views (External Identifiers section)
capabilities.test: 6 external identifier types + a revocation of the DOI
capabilities.observed: 7 external references; DOI shows revoked/stop=true; unknown scheme "future-pid-type-xyz" retained=true; TII still valid=true
capabilities.limitation: The system associates external identifiers as data. It does NOT resolve, dereference, or validate any of them — a recorded DOI is the recorder's assertion, not proof the DOI exists (see §42). Revocation/disappearance is recorded as an act; the reference stays in history.

capabilities.capability: §36 Non-scholarly objects — paper history / software / dataset / physical artifact / sensor series / institutional rule / disputed classification / no-file
capabilities.test: 8 structurally different reference kinds, each a TII with one arbitrary module record
capabilities.observed: all 8 project as valid TIIs with no schema change=true; 8 distinct identifiers issued
capabilities.limitation: None. The thin core has no object-category field. "document", "dataset", "sensor" etc. are just module names chosen by the recorder. TII is not a paper identifier.

capabilities.capability: §37 "No object" — a TII tracing a disputed/divergent reference without asserting one stable object
capabilities.test: issue a TII, record two incompatible observations + an interpretation refusing a single referent + a classification dispute
capabilities.observed: TII valid with no object field=true; two divergent observations + interpretation recorded=true
capabilities.limitation: None. There is no permanent object/referent field. Issuing a TII asserts only "tracking started from this reference point" (SPEC §1).

capabilities.capability: §38 Category removal — withdraw a "document"/"state"/"transition"/"ignition"/"domain"/"lineage" classification; historical records stay parsable
capabilities.test: for each category: introduce then withdraw; export → re-import → project → verify
capabilities.observed: all 6 categories: withdraw recorded, records still project, chain still verifies=true
capabilities.limitation: None. Withdrawing a classification is a normal event. The withdrawn bucket still shows in history with a "withdrawn" flag; nothing becomes unparsable.

capabilities.capability: §39 Audit-of-the-audit — an audit judgment can itself be corrected / contested / withdrawn / superseded / translated / evidenced; no privileged "final audit"
capabilities.codePath: src/ledger.append (audit is just a module), src/projection, displayContent
capabilities.test: an audit.judged event + correction + dispute + withdrawal + localization
capabilities.observed: no privileged final-audit type exists=true; audit judgment is corrigible/contestable/withdrawable=true; audit finding is translatable=true
capabilities.limitation: None. "audit" is an ordinary module. The engine gives no event_type special or terminal status.

capabilities.capability: §40 Privacy boundary — what happens to content that should not be public
capabilities.codePath: no privacy code exists in src/
capabilities.test: append an event with a "restricted" disclosure hint + sensitive text; check every output surface
capabilities.observed: disclosure:"restricted" hint is IGNORED. Secret string appears in: canonical JSONL=true, JSON export=true, CSV export=true, resolution HTML=true, static site=true, projection/API shape=true
capabilities.limitation: The current system publishes every field of every event on every surface. There is no disclosure classification, no commitment/redaction mechanism, no access control on reads. Anything written to an event is public. This is an OPEN PRODUCTION ISSUE by design (the model is specified but not built).

capabilities.capability: §22/§23 Candidate 26-char production identifier — generation, 128-bit round trip, canonical form, rejections, fragment separation, resolver URL, distribution
capabilities.layer: B (candidate — NOT connected to live issuance)
capabilities.codePath: src/candidate/identifier.js (imported by nothing in the running system)
capabilities.test: 20,000 generated tokens + ~16 targeted parse checks; coarse byte-value histogram (32 bins)
capabilities.observed: {"valid_generation":true,"roundtrip_128bit":true,"lowercase_canonical":true,"uppercase_accepted":true,"reject_bad_char_0":true,"reject_bad_char_1":true,"reject_padding":true,"reject_non_canonical_tail":true,"reject_whitespace":true,"reject_unicode":true,"reject_query":true,"fragment_separated":true,"canonical_form_rejects_fragment":true,"resolver_url":true,"repeated_canonicalization_idempotent":true,"distribution_sanity":true}; histogram max deviation from mean = 2.36%
capabilities.limitation: CANDIDATE ONLY. src/id.js still issues the provisional 12-char Crockford token. This code is not on any live path. §23 collision-retry: candId.issueIdentifier(exists) discards a collided candidate before recording — covered by test/candidate-identifier.test.js "issuance discards a collided candidate"; still CANDIDATE ONLY.

capabilities.capability: §24 Candidate signed checkpoints — Ed25519 + RFC 8785 JCS: signature validity, tamper detection, property-order/whitespace independence, duplicate-key rejection, key rotation, revocation
capabilities.layer: B (candidate — NOT wired into the live path)
capabilities.codePath: src/candidate/checkpoint.js + src/candidate/jcs.js (imported by nothing in the running system)
capabilities.test: 13 checkpoint checks incl. rotation and revocation
capabilities.observed: {"valid_signature":true,"changed_head_fails":true,"changed_count_fails":true,"changed_time_fails":true,"reordered_props_ok":true,"whitespace_irrelevant":true,"duplicate_props_rejected":true,"malformed_sig_fails":true,"wrong_key_fails":true,"export_reimport_ok":true,"rotation_old_still_verifies":true,"revoked_key_policy":true}
capabilities.limitation: CANDIDATE ONLY. The LIVE service produces NO signed checkpoints. Nothing in src/server.js, src/export.js, or bin/tii.js signs anything. Ledger authenticity today rests entirely on the SHA-256 chain, which does not attest authorship (see §26).

capabilities.capability: §25 Ledger tampering detection (single edits / delete / reorder / dup / hash edits / chain break)
capabilities.test: 10 tamper cases on disposable copies
capabilities.observed: {"modify_one_historical_byte":{"detected":true,"problems":["content hash mismatch (event body altered)"]},"modify_one_historical_field_recorder":{"detected":true,"problems":["content hash mismatch (event body altered)"]},"remove_one_event":{"detected":true,"problems":["seq 3 != position 2","prev_hash does not match previous event hash","seq 4 != position 3","seq 5 != position 4"]},"reorder_two_events":{"detected":true,"problems":["seq 3 != position 2","prev_hash does not match previous event hash","seq 2 != position 3","prev_hash does not match previous event hash","prev_hash does not match previous event hash"]},"duplicate_an_event":{"detected":true,"problems":["seq 3 != position 4","prev_hash does not match previous event hash","seq 4 != position 5","seq 5 != position 6"]},"change_prev_hash":{"detected":true,"problems":["prev_hash does not match previous event hash","content hash mismatch (event body altered)"]},"change_current_hash":{"detected":true,"problems":["content hash mismatch (event body altered)","prev_hash does not match previous event hash"]},"truncate_final_line":{"detected":true,"problems":["load threw: Unterminated string in JSON at position 491 (line 1 column 492)"]},"append_malformed_json":{"detected":true,"problems":["load threw: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)"]},"append_valid_json_no_chain_link":{"detected":true,"problems":["prev_hash does not match previous event hash","content hash mismatch (event body altered)"]}}
capabilities.limitation: A truncated/malformed final line makes load() THROW (whole ledger unparsable) rather than returning a graceful verify() problem. verify() is not run automatically on load.

capabilities.capability: §26 Full-chain regeneration attack — can verify() alone detect a fully-recomputed forged chain?
capabilities.test: rewrite event #2 in a disposable copy, recompute the entire SHA-256 chain, run verify()
capabilities.observed: forged chain verify.ok=true; verify cannot distinguish forged from legit=true; candidate signed checkpoint DOES detect it (true)
capabilities.limitation: verify() proves internal consistency, NOT authenticity or non-rewriting. Anyone with write access to (or serving a copy of) ledger.jsonl can rewrite history undetectably by verify() alone. Detection requires an independently-published signed checkpoint / external timestamp — CANDIDATE ONLY, not wired in.

capabilities.capability: §27 Crash consistency
capabilities.test: partial final line; duplicate identical request
capabilities.observed: {"partial_line_on_load":"load() THROWS: Unterminated string in JSON at position 57 (line 1 column 58)  → the ENTIRE ledger fails to load; the last complete write is not recoverable without manual truncation","terminate_before_write":"fs.appendFileSync is synchronous and atomic for small writes on local fs: either the whole line lands or nothing does. A crash BEFORE the syscall loses that one event with no corruption.","terminate_mid_write":"A crash DURING the syscall (large line, disk full, signal) can leave a partial final line → see partial_line_on_load: the whole ledger then fails to parse on next start.","duplicate_request":"two identical append() calls produce TWO events (evt_yn8vx13s36mf15vr and evt_djex84fe8jwhra73), both with content.text \"same request\", different seq/event_id/hash. There is NO idempotency key, dedup, or request-id. verify() stays ok. A client that retries after a lost response silently double-records."}
capabilities.limitation: A partial/interrupted final write makes the ENTIRE ledger fail to load (JSON.parse throws) until the line is manually removed. No fsync, no atomic rename, no journaling, no tail recovery. Client retries after a lost response silently double-record (no idempotency key).

capabilities.capability: §29 Clock behaviour
capabilities.test: backward / far-future / missing / tz-offset timestamps
capabilities.observed: seq (append order), not wall-clock. projection sorts by e.seq. Event order in history = [1,2,3,4,5] i.e. append order regardless of the nonsensical recorded_at values.
capabilities.limitation: Ordering is by append seq, NOT wall clock — integrity-safe. But recorded_at is unvalidated and timezone offsets are not normalised to UTC, so a bad client clock shows misleading dates on the resolution page.

capabilities.capability: §21 Input security — code-shaped content cannot execute or corrupt output
capabilities.codePath: src/views.esc (escapes & < > "), address links gated by /^https?:/ + esc-quoted href
capabilities.test: 22 payloads (script/svg/js-url/attr-breakout/traversal/etc.) across all HTML + export surfaces; see spec/security-test-results.md
capabilities.observed: no execution or structural-corruption path found; inert NUL/bidi pass-through only
capabilities.limitation: Minor: raw NUL / C0 / bidi characters pass through into HTML/JSON as inert text (not stripped or flagged). No CSP header. GET /admin/hash-file is an arbitrary-server-file-read primitive, open when TII_ADMIN_TOKEN is unset.

capabilities.capability: §28 Concurrency — multiple OS processes writing one ledger.jsonl
capabilities.test: spawn 2 / 10 / 100 separate processes each appending 10 events to the same file
capabilities.observed: [{"writers":2,"dup_seq":1,"chain_breaks":1,"verify_ok":false},{"writers":10,"dup_seq":31,"chain_breaks":44,"verify_ok":false},{"writers":100,"dup_seq":457,"chain_breaks":384,"verify_ok":false}]
capabilities.limitation: The JSONL ledger is SINGLE-WRITER ONLY. Concurrent processes produce duplicate seq numbers, broken prev_hash links, corrupt lines, lost updates, verify() failure. In-process concurrency is safe (append() has no await). Current production avoids this by being a read-only static mirror (zero writes).

capabilities.capability: §30/§31 Scale & large payloads
capabilities.codePath: src/ledger (all events in memory), src/projection (O(events) forTII scan), src/export.buildStaticSite (no index/pagination/incremental)
capabilities.test: 100/1000/10000 TIIs; 1KB–10MB payloads
capabilities.observed: at 10000 TIIs / 50000 events: issue 5983/s, append 7777/s, verify 151723 ev/s, single lookup 0.83ms, registry render 7061ms, rebuild-static 11007ms, ledger 26.29MB, heap +239.7MB. A 10MB inline payload → ~19.5MB resolution HTML.
capabilities.limitation: Everything is O(events) and fully in memory. Registry render is O(all events) per request (~7s at 10k TIIs). rebuild-static is a full rebuild every time (~11s at 10k TIIs). No index, pagination, incremental build, or streaming. Ledger ~2.6KB/event ⇒ ~260MB at 100k events; heap ~13GB projected at 1M TIIs. Large evidence must be referenced (hash + address), not stored inline (practical inline limit ~100KB).

capabilities.capability: §32 Reconstruction from exports alone
capabilities.test: export ledger.jsonl only; fresh dir with src/+bin/+Node; run CLI + rebuild-static + re-project
capabilities.observed: {"all_tii_strings":true,"head_hash_identical":true,"verify_ok":true,"event_count_identical":true,"localization_survived":true,"authored_ja_survived":true,"external_id_survived":true,"optional_modules_survived":true,"unknown_vocab_survived":true,"evidence_survived":true,"public_pages_rebuilt":true}
capabilities.limitation: None. Zero npm dependencies; no DB/service state. Identifiers, events, hashes, localizations, external ids, unknown vocab, evidence, and public pages all survive.

capabilities.capability: §33 Hosting loss (Vercel disappears)
capabilities.test: run CLI + rebuild-static with no hosting
capabilities.observed: PASS — hosting is not identity.
capabilities.limitation: One env var (TII_RESOLVER_BASE_URL) + redeploy. Hosting is not identity.

capabilities.capability: §34 Domain loss model
capabilities.layer: A live for identifier/records; C spec-only for signed checkpoints & mirror protocol
capabilities.test: what remains usable if the future permanent domain is unavailable
capabilities.observed: {"raw tii:<token>":"YES — it is a string; it contains no domain","exported registry (ledger.jsonl / catalog.json)":"YES — self-contained","signed checkpoint":"CANDIDATE ONLY — not produced by the live system","independent mirrors":"CONCEPT ONLY — no mirror protocol implemented; a mirror is just another copy of ledger.jsonl","local reconstruction":"YES — demonstrated in §32"}
capabilities.limitation: Identifier + exported records survive a domain loss now. Signed checkpoints and a mirror protocol are CANDIDATE / CONCEPT ONLY. Spec URL, role emails, IANA reference all need the (unchosen) permanent domain.

capabilities.capability: §35 Complete operator loss (institute + hosting + registrar + maintainers gone)
capabilities.test: what a third party could reconstruct from public spec + exported ledger + source + independent copies
capabilities.observed: identifiers + full record + derived state + chain self-consistency all reconstructable; NOT: proof the ledger was not rewritten before receipt, domain/registrar recovery, continued checkpoint signing, IANA change-controller role
capabilities.limitation: The IDENTIFIERS and the RECORD survive completely. The TRUST ANCHOR (live signed checkpoint / external timestamp) and the GOVERNANCE + DOMAIN CUSTODY do not exist yet — succession is documented, not implemented.

phase1_production_hardening_update.note: Appended by production-hardening Phase 1. The 'capabilities' array above is UNCHANGED from the original audit run — nothing above was edited or reworded. This block records before/repair/after for the specific items this phase touched (P0-A/B/C, P1); see spec/production-hardening-phase1.md for the full report and spec/capability-boundary-audit.md for the prose version of this same update.

updates.after_status: PASS (A - live core), conditional on a configured signing key
updates.repair: src/candidate/checkpoint.js + src/candidate/jcs.js promoted to src/checkpoint.js + src/jcs.js; wired into src/checkpoint-store.js, bin/tii.js checkpoint create/verify/list/keygen, GET /status, GET /checkpoint/verify, GET /checkpoint/list, GET /audit, and an auto-checkpoint-on-write hook in src/server.js.
updates.still_true: With no signing key configured (TII_CHECKPOINT_PRIVATE_KEY / _FILE unset), checkpoint creation fails closed (NoSigningKeyError) and no checkpoint is produced. Reads are unaffected.

updates.after_status: FAIL unchanged for claim A alone (by design); PASS for the combined claim A+B posture, conditional on a signing key being configured before the forgery occurs
updates.repair: Live checkpoints (see §24 above). Permanent regression test test/checkpoint-store.test.js test C forges a full chain and asserts verify().ok===true (claim A still fooled) AND verifyCheckpoint(...).matches_current_head===false against a legitimately pre-signed checkpoint (claim B catches it). Required to remain permanently in the suite.
updates.still_true: Without a configured signing key, or if the attacker's rewrite happens before any checkpoint was ever created, this attack is exactly as undetectable as before. A checkpoint only protects against forgery of history that predates it.

updates.before_status: open when TII_ADMIN_TOKEN unset (authorized() returned true with no token)
updates.repair: authorized() in src/server.js now returns false unconditionally when TII_ADMIN_TOKEN is unset (NO ADMIN TOKEN = ADMIN DISABLED). Independently, hash-file now requires an operator-configured TII_ADMIN_HASH_DIR and rejects any path resolving outside it (resolveSafeHashPath()), even with a valid token.
updates.still_true: n/a - this sub-finding is fully closed. Verified by test/admin-security.test.js (6 tests).

updates.after_status: PARTIAL (unchanged status; underlying failure mode repaired, new documented cost)
updates.repair: Write-ahead journal (<ledger>.journal) + double fsync per append (journal, then ledger); explicit non-silent recovery detection (Ledger.load uses parseLedgerTolerant, sets recovery.required, stops writable mode); operator-invoked recovery commands (tii recover inspect/truncate-tail/commit-journal/discard-journal); idempotency-key mechanism for issueTII and append.
updates.still_true: A truncated/malformed tail still requires explicit operator action to repair (by design - never auto-healed). New cost: append throughput dropped from ~7,800-9,800/s to ~98/s (~10.2ms/append, measured on this hardware) due to the two fsync calls per append - this is a deliberate, disclosed tradeoff, not an oversight.

updates.capability_ref: §28 Concurrency - multiple OS processes writing one ledger.jsonl
updates.after_status: PASS (A - live core) for the single-writer model specifically
updates.repair: Cross-process advisory locking (src/writer-lock.js, O_EXCL-based, stale-lock reclaim, bounded retry) plus a resync-under-lock fix (Ledger._resyncIfChanged) for a bug found during this phase's own testing: a lock alone does not stop a writer computing conflicting event fields from a stale in-memory snapshot.
